title: Crispy Ginger Chicken Thighs
description: Boneless chicken thighs seared until the edges go crunchy, then lacquered in a sticky ginger-soy glaze that caramelizes in the pan. Twenty-five minutes, one skillet, and dinner that tastes like you tried harder than you did.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: from a 3-inch piece, peeled and finely grated

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, garlic, and cornstarch together in a small bowl until smooth. Set this sauce aside.
Pat chicken thighs very dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking.

Add chicken thighs in a single layer — work in batches to avoid crowding. Cook without moving until the underside is deeply golden and crisp, 5 to 6 minutes. Flip and cook until cooked through, another 4 to 5 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Pour the sauce mixture into the skillet and stir, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Let it simmer and thicken until glossy and syrupy, 1 to 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan and turn to coat in the glaze. Serve over steamed rice, spooning extra sauce over the top. Finish with scallions and sesame seeds.

inspirations.author: BA Test Kitchen
inspirations.note: Inspired by BA's approach to pan-crisped chicken with Asian glazes, a weeknight staple of the test kitchen
